1-1-systems-architecture.alt: Von Neumann architecture diagram: the CPU, containing registers, control unit and ALU, connected to main memory by the address, data and control buses
1-1-systems-architecture.caption: Von Neumann architecture. The CPU and main memory exchange addresses and data over buses, and instructions and data share the same memory.

1-1-systems-architecture.alt: Photograph of a desktop CPU package
1-1-systems-architecture.caption: The physical CPU, a desktop processor package.

1-2-memory-storage.alt: Photograph of a RAM memory module
1-2-memory-storage.caption: A RAM module. Primary storage is fast and volatile, holding running programs and their data.

1-2-memory-storage.alt: Diagram of the surface of an optical disc showing pits and lands and the binary data they encode
1-2-memory-storage.caption: Optical storage records data as pits and lands. Each transition between them is read as a 1.

1-2-memory-storage.alt: A grid of ones and zeros shown as black and white pixels, illustrating how a bitmap image is stored in binary
1-2-memory-storage.caption: A bitmap is just binary. Each pixel's colour is stored as a binary value, here 1 bit per pixel.

1-2-memory-storage.alt: An analogue sound wave with sample points marked at regular time intervals
1-2-memory-storage.caption: Sampling. The analogue wave is measured at regular intervals, and each sample is stored as a binary number.

1-2-memory-storage.alt: The full ASCII character table with decimal and 7-bit binary codes for each character
1-2-memory-storage.caption: The ASCII character set. Each character maps to a 7-bit binary code.

1-3-networks.alt: Star topology diagram: eight computers each cabled to one central switch
1-3-networks.caption: Star topology. Every device connects to a central switch, so one failed cable isolates only one device.

1-3-networks.alt: Two mesh network diagrams, a partial mesh on the left and a fully connected mesh on the right
1-3-networks.caption: Mesh topologies, partial on the left and full on the right. Every node has more than one route to the others.

1-3-networks.alt: Diagram of nine routers between a sender and receiver, showing the many routes a packet can take
1-3-networks.caption: Packet switching. Routers pass packets from sender to receiver, and each packet can take a different route.

1-3-networks.alt: The four network layers stacked: application, transport, internet and link
1-3-networks.caption: Protocol layers. Each layer has one job and passes data only to the layer above or below it.

1-4-network-security.alt: Sketchnote of social engineering themes: access, login, spying, fraud, passwords, security, influence and pretext
1-4-network-security.caption: Social engineering targets the person, not the machine.

1-4-network-security.alt: A phishing text message offering a fake tax refund with a fraudulent HMRC link
1-4-network-security.caption: A phishing text. Urgency, a refund hook and a fake HMRC web address.

1-4-network-security.alt: Diagram of a firewall as a brick wall between a LAN and the wider network
1-4-network-security.caption: A firewall sits between the LAN and the wider network, filtering traffic in both directions.

1-5-systems-software.alt: A grid of numbered coloured blocks scattered across a disk, representing fragmented files
1-5-systems-software.caption: A fragmented disk holds files in scattered blocks. Defragmentation reorders them so each file is contiguous and faster to read.

1-6-impacts.alt: Circular diagram of a device's lifecycle: resource extraction, manufacturing, transportation, use and end-of-life recycling
1-6-impacts.caption: The device lifecycle. Every stage, from resource extraction to disposal, carries an environmental cost.

1-6-impacts.alt: Photograph of a large pile of discarded electronic equipment
1-6-impacts.caption: E-waste. Discarded devices hold both toxic materials and recoverable metals.

2-1-algorithms.alt: A sorted list of numbers one to nine with low, mid and high pointers marked for binary search
2-1-algorithms.caption: Binary search. The low, mid and high pointers halve the search space with each comparison. The list must already be sorted.

2-1-algorithms.alt: Merge sort trace: a list of eight numbers repeatedly split into halves, then merged back together in sorted order
2-1-algorithms.caption: Merge sort. Split the list until each part holds one item, then merge the parts back together in order.

2-3-robust-programs.alt: Two circles labelled Code and Test joined by arrows in a loop
2-3-robust-programs.caption: Iterative testing. Code and test alternate in a loop all the way through development.

2-3-robust-programs.alt: A reCAPTCHA checkbox reading I'm not a robot
2-3-robust-programs.caption: Authentication in defensive design. A CAPTCHA checks the user is human before input is accepted.

2-4-boolean-logic.alt: AND gate truth table shown physically: two switches in series light a bulb only when both are closed, beside gate symbols for all four input pairs
2-4-boolean-logic.caption: The AND gate. Output is 1 only when both inputs are 1, shown here as switches and a bulb.

2-4-boolean-logic.alt: OR gate truth table shown physically: the bulb lights when either switch is closed, beside gate symbols for all four input pairs
2-4-boolean-logic.caption: The OR gate. Output is 1 when at least one input is 1.

2-4-boolean-logic.alt: Logic circuit with inputs A, B and C passing through an AND gate and an OR gate into another OR gate, then a NOT gate, to output Q
2-4-boolean-logic.caption: A logic circuit built from AND, OR and NOT gates. Trace each input combination through to Q.
